question: What is the main purpose of using a partograph during labor?

options.A: To replace the need for physical abdominal examinations
options.B: To monitor labor progress and detect complications early
options.C: To calculate the exact date and time of conception
options.D: To record the financial cost of hospital admission

explanation: The partograph gives midwives a clear visual guide of how labor is moving, helping spot warning signs before they become dangerous emergencies. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why is the partograph considered especially useful in busy Nigerian maternity units?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any documentation by doctors
options.B: It guarantees that every birth will be completely painless
options.C: It allows women to discharge themselves from the ward
options.D: It acts as an early warning system to guide prompt referrals

explanation: By tracking labor visually, midwives can quickly see when a patient needs higher-level care long before severe distress sets in. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h1)

question: At what minimum cervical dilation should a routine partograph be started?
explanation: Starting the partograph at four centimeters marks the official entry into the active phase of first-stage labor. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h2)

question: A primigravida arrives at the labor ward with a 2 cm dilated cervix and mild irregular contractions. What is the correct immediate action?

options.A: Open a partograph immediately and prepare for emergency delivery
options.B: Wait and monitor her in the first stage area until active labor begins
options.C: Transfer her straight to the operating theater for a cesarean section
options.D: Administer oxytocin drip to speed up her cervical dilation

explanation: Because she is still in the latent phase with a cervix less than four centimeters, starting a partograph now is incorrect and could lead to false alarms. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h2)

question: How often should the fetal heart rate be checked and recorded on the partograph during the active phase?
explanation: Checking the fetal heart rate every half hour allows the midwife to spot signs of fetal distress quickly. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h3)

question: What does a moulding score of plus-plus (++) signify during a vaginal examination?

options.A: Fetal skull bones are overlapping but can still be separated
options.B: Fetal skull bones are widely separated with wide sutures
options.C: There is severe, irreducible overlap indicating disproportion
options.D: The membranes are intact and bulging with clear fluid

explanation: Double plus moulding means the bones are touching and overlapping, but pressure can still push them back into place, showing moderate adaptation. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h3)

question: How often should a vaginal examination be performed to assess cervical dilation during normal active labor?
explanation: A four-hourly vaginal examination balances tracking progress with minimizing the risk of introducing infection into the birth canal. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which of the following vital signs is monitored more frequently than the others on the partograph?
explanation: Pulse rate is checked every 30 minutes to catch early signs of maternal exhaustion, dehydration, or hemorrhage, while temperature and blood pressure are checked every four hours. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h4)

question: At what rate does the alert line on the partograph progress upward?
explanation: The alert line is drawn assuming normal cervical dilation proceeds at a steady pace of one centimeter every hour during the active phase. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h5)

question: What clinical action is required when a laboring woman's cervical dilation graph crosses over the action line?

options.A: Immediate intervention and definitive management for prolonged labor
options.B: Discharge the patient home because labor has slowed down
options.C: Wait another four hours to see if labor picks up on its own
options.D: Stop all fetal monitoring and encourage the mother to sleep

explanation: Crossing the action line means labor is dangerously prolonged, requiring prompt medical review, such as augmentation or cesarean delivery. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why must a midwife evaluate all parameters on the partograph together rather than looking at cervical dilation alone?

options.A: Fetal condition and maternal status greatly influence the safety of ongoing labor
options.B: Doctors will refuse to read the chart if any section is blank
options.C: Cervical dilation is never an accurate indicator of labor progress
options.D: Hospital policy requires every single box on the paper to contain ink

explanation: Progress in dilation means little if the baby is showing signs of severe distress or the mother is developing signs of infection or exhaustion. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h6)

question: A midwife notes that a patient at a primary health clinic has crossed the alert line. What is the appropriate next step?

options.A: Tear up the partograph and start a fresh page the next morning
options.B: Advise the woman to walk around the compound for two hours
options.C: Arrange prompt transfer to a facility with emergency obstetric care
options.D: Perform an immediate vacuum extraction in the primary clinic

explanation: Crossing the alert line at a primary center serves as a warning sign requiring referral before the situation deteriorates to the action line. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h6)
